Write learned gating strategies as a Gating-ML 2.0 document

Source: R/export-gates.R
write_gating_ml.Rd

Each strategy becomes a chain of polygon gates, level n declared as the child of level n-1, which is what makes the file a gating STRATEGY rather than a bag of regions: software reading it applies them in the order they were learned, on the cells the previous gate kept.

Usage

write_gating_ml(
  polygons,
  path,
  transform,
  id_col = "label",
  x_col = "x_transformed",
  y_col = "y_transformed",
  n_per_edge = 24L,
  channel_map = NULL,
  space = c("transformed", "linear"),
  compensation_ref = c("FCS", "uncompensated", "supplied"),
  spillover = NULL,
  M = 4.5
)

Arguments

polygons

a polygons table from explain_external_labels() or explain_unmatched_clusters()

path

destination .xml

transform

the transform object the run used

id_col

column naming the strategy each row belongs to

x_col, y_col

columns holding the vertex coordinates

n_per_edge

edge subdivision passed to polygon_to_linear(), for space = "linear"

channel_map

optional named character vector, marker symbol to the files' $PnN; required with compensation_ref = "supplied"

space

"transformed" (default where the transform has a Gating-ML form) or "linear"

compensation_ref

"FCS" (default), "uncompensated" or "supplied"; see above

spillover

for compensation_ref = "supplied", the spillover matrix the files were compensated with, the files' $PnN as its column names (see gating_ml_spillover())

M

decades for the Gating-ML asinh parameters. Any positive value states the same transform; 4.5 matches the logicle default.

Value

path, invisibly, or NULL when there was nothing to write

Details

COORDINATES ARE ON THE ANALYSIS SCALE by default: one Gating-ML transformation per marker (fasinh for arcsinh, logicle for logicle) and each vertex divided into its units, which states the fitted region exactly. space = "linear" writes the region in the units the FCS file stores instead, edges subdivided before inversion.

COMPENSATION. A gate drawn on data compensated with the file's own $SPILLOVER is declared compensation-ref="FCS", which tells the reader to apply that same matrix; data with no matrix in the file, already unmixed by the acquisition software, are declared uncompensated. The earlier export declared every gate uncompensated, which told readers to gate the stored, uncompensated values for gates cyRAVEN had placed on compensated ones. Data compensated with a matrix from --spillover ("supplied") carry that matrix in the document as a spectrumMatrix, and each gate dimension it compensated references its identifier, as Gating-ML 2.0 section 7 defines: "FCS" would tell the reader to apply each file's own $SPILLOVER, the matrix the run replaced. A dimension whose detector the matrix does not hold was never compensated and is declared uncompensated.

READING "FCS" WITH flowCore. A reader applying an "FCS" gate fetches each file's $SPILLOVER itself. flowCore 2.18 to 2.22, every release up to Bioconductor 3.22, stops there on R 4.2 or later ("the condition has length > 1": getSpilloverFromFlowFrame() tests class(mySpill) != "matrix", and a matrix has two classes since R 4.0); the fix (!is(mySpill, "matrix"), upstream commit 903b5b3) is in flowCore 2.25 (Bioconductor devel), and the cyRAVEN image installs 2.18.0 with it (inst/scripts/patch_flowcore.R). Checked with flowUtils 1.63.0: on the patched 2.18 the three cases apply and count exactly the events computed directly.

DIMENSION NAMES. Gating-ML 2.0 names a dimension of an FCS file by its $PnN (section 4.1), also under "FCS" (4.2.2), so channel_map should map each marker symbol to the files' $PnN (gating_ml_markers()); without it the marker symbols are written, which no FCS file holds as a column name. Under a spectrumMatrix a compensated dimension is named by its fluorochrome instead (7.3), here the marker symbol, prefixed Comp- where it would equal a detector name, which section 7.2 forbids; a detector carrying no marker of the run is Comp- and its $PnN.
